newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-RENOWNED DEFENDER GOUGH JOINING MLS WIZARDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RENOWNED DEFENDER GOUGH JOINING MLS WIZARDS.

text.p: Veteran defender and Glasgow Rangers captain Richard Gough will be moving to Major League Soccer in May and joining the Kansas City Wizards of the professional U.S. league.
No financial terms of the deal were disclosed, but the team said the 34-year-old Gough will join the Wizards at the conclusion of the Scottish Premier League season.
Gough will be reunited with former Rangers teammate and compatriot Mo Johnston in Kansas City.

"This is a major, major acquisition for Kansas City and Major League Soccer," said coach Ron Newman in a statement Tuesday. "Richard Gough is one of the most respected players in European football and he is at the top of his game."
Gough has 61 caps with Scotland and has been on nine Scottish League championship teams.
"I'm coming to the U.S. for a new challenge and to help the Wizards win the league championship," Gough said. "That's what motivates me.
"I had a lot of offers from Europe and Japan, but I have been impressed with Major League Soccer. Mo Johnston has spoken very highly of both Kansas City and the calibre of play in the league."
Kansas City had the league's worst defensive record last season, giving up 63 goals or nearly two a game.
Gough, who has played the last 10 years with Rangers after beginning his career with Dundee United, also has won three Scottish Cups and six League Cup winners' medals.
